text: Vietnam exported 108,800 tons of coffee worth $501.2 million in October 2026, up 53.2% in volume and 22.9% in value year-on-year, according to the Vietnam Customs.
However, the average export price fell 19.8% from October 2025 to $4,606 per ton, despite edging up 1.9% from September.
In the first 10 months of 2026, coffee exports totalled 1.56 million tons, generating $7.08 billion.

While volume increased 18.5% year-on-year, export value declined 5.2%, mainly due to an approximately 20% drop in average prices as supplies from the new harvest began to increase, putting downward pressure on domestic and international markets.
The European Union remained Vietnam's largest coffee market, accounting for 40.9% of export value.
Shipments to the bloc reached 681,800 tons worth $2.89 billion, up 25% in volume but down 3.9% in value year-on-year.
Exports to the United States rose 47% in volume and 15.7% in value to 109,800 tons and $471.1 million, respectively.
Demand from Russia and China also strengthened.
Vietnam shipped 83,700 tons to Russia, up 30.3%, and 59,900 tons to China, up 49%.
The Vietnam Coffee-Cocoa Association (Vicofa) forecasts that full-year export volume could increase 8-10% from 2025, supported by improved supplies as the new harvest gets under way in late November.
